topic.title: [Microsurgical hair transplantation - safe and sustainable]
topic.abstract: A hair transplant may restore advanced androgenetic alopecia or scalp scars. Suitable patients have sufficient donor hair, at least for their current stage of alopecia. The planning of the hair line, graft number, and hair distribution should be sustainable as the alopecia may progress and the donor hair is limited. Hair-preserving medications are therefore recommended. Digital trichoscopy and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted hair measurements may aid in the assessment of the recipient and donor area and help to exclude inflammatory hair and scalp conditions. The procedure is performed in local anaesthesia and consists of several manual steps, using microsurgical instruments and loupe magnification. In most cases, each follicular unit containing 1-4 hairs is harvested individually using special micropunches (follicular unit excision, FUE). Each skin cut should be performed by the operating hair surgeon. This includes the nontraumatic excision of the follicular units and the creation of recipient sites in a natural direction, followed by a careful graft insertion. Automated devices may assist the hair surgeon. For a successful procedure, an individual treatment plan, careful graft handling and follow-up care by the hair surgeon are crucial. Referring dermatologists should advise patients, especially when they are younger, to prefer a nonaggressive surgical and individually tailored approach as well as concomitant medical therapy. A procedure which is not performed professionally, especially by nonlicensed personnel, may carry several aesthetic and medical risks. On the other hand, a well-done microsurgical hair transplantation may lead to a long-lasting natural hair restoration.
